newsitem.title: USA: Prospects for Iraqi oil sales deflates U.S. crudes.
newsitem.headline: Prospects for Iraqi oil sales deflates U.S. crudes.

text.p: Cash crude prices in the U.S. Gulf deflated Thursday morning after Iraqi Oil Minister Amir Muhammad Rasheed reiterated that he expected renewed Iraqi oil sales within 10 days.

Rasheed, speaking from Vienna where he attended the now concluded OPEC meeting, also said there was no linkeage between oil sales and aid distribution under the second round of "oil-for-food" accord dealings.
The softer tone expressed by Rasheed left cash traders expecting Iraqi exports to hit the market again by mid-July, eliminating a source of some bullishness.

Outright August West Texas Intermediate/Cushing was 40 cents weaker at $19.10-20 a barrel. Traders said August Exchange for Physicals were pegged about five cents over the NYMEX screen, though EFP dealings were scarce.
July cash business ended on Wednesday, leaving the market deflated and quiet for the start of August grade trade.
Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James barrels were pegged around a 10 cents premium to the August benchmark, with Midland/WTI steady from Wednesday at 30-35 cents under the marker.
Sour crudes were also steady at a $1.35 discount for West Texas Sour/Midland parcels, and Eugene Island around $1.40-45 under the marker.
